jp: 社員[しゃいん]{は|wa-topic}田中[たなか]さん{と|to-and}山田[やまだ]さん、二人[ふたり]だけです。
en: The staff are just Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Yamada, only two people.
why: The two names are the complete list, so と is needed; や would suggest more people.

jp: 同僚[どうりょう]{と|to-and}私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}どちらも新入社員[しんにゅうしゃいん]です。
en: My colleague and I are both new employees.
why: どちらも (both) needs the complete-list と; か would mean one or the other.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{と|to-and}数学[すうがく]、両方[りょうほう]あります。
en: There is homework in both English and math.
why: 両方 (both) requires と, which joins exactly these two subjects.

jp: この学校[がっこう]{に|ni-location}{は|wa-contrast}アメリカ{と|to-and}中国[ちゅうごく]、両方[りょうほう]{の|no-possessive}留学生[りゅうがくせい]{が|ga-existence}います。
en: This school has students from both America and China.
why: 両方 (both) needs と for the complete pair; か would mean one or the other.

jp: かばん{に|ni-location}{は|wa-contrast}教科書[きょうかしょ]{や|ya-list}ノート{が|ga-existence}入[はい]っています。
en: My bag has things like textbooks and notebooks in it.
why: Textbooks and notebooks are only examples of what is in the bag, so the open-list や is right; と would be the full list.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{で|de-place}田中[たなか]さん{や|ya-list}山田[やまだ]さん{が|ga-subject}意見[いけん]{を|o-object}言[い]いました。
en: At the meeting, people like Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Yamada gave their opinions.
why: The two names are only examples of who spoke, so や is right; と would mean exactly those two.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{の|no-possessive}あと、図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}宿題[しゅくだい]{や|ya-list}予習[よしゅう]{を|o-object}します。
en: After class I do things like homework and preparation at the library.
why: Homework and preparation are examples of what I do, so the open-list や fits; と would make them the whole list.

jp: レポート{は|wa-topic}月曜日[げつようび]{か|ka-or}火曜日[かようび]{に|ni-time}出[だ]してください。
en: Please hand in the report on Monday or Tuesday.
why: Monday and Tuesday are alternatives, so か means 'or'; と would ask for it on both days.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]、一時間[いちじかん]{か|ka-or}二時間[にじかん]勉強[べんきょう]します。
en: I study for an hour or two every day.
why: A rough amount, 'one or two hours', joins the numbers with か; と and や cannot give an approximate range.

jp: 佐藤[さとう]さん{か|ka-or}鈴木[すずき]さん{が|ga-subject}明日[あした]{の|no-possessive}会議[かいぎ]{に|ni-destination}出[で]ます。
en: Either Ms. Sato or Mr. Suzuki will attend tomorrow's meeting.
why: Only one of the two will attend, so か means 'or'; と would send both of them.
